newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK MAGISTRATE ORDERS BROKERS TO OPEN ACCOUNTS.
newsitem.headline: GREEK MAGISTRATE ORDERS BROKERS TO OPEN ACCOUNTS.

text.p: A Greek magistrate, investigating the Delta Securities scandal, has ordered all 65 bourse members to reveal whether 16 specific clients had accounts with them and to supply their trading history from January 1, 1996.

"Acting on the prosecutor's order and in the course of our investigation we ask that you supply us with (this) information by November 26, 1996 at the latest," magistrate Costas Ganiatsos said in a letter to the Athens brokerages.
This means all brokers will have to reveal to the magistrate
whether anyone on the list of 16 individuals or corporations had
accounts with them and what their trading history has been since
Effectively, this means account numbers must be opened.
This will allow the magistrate to cross check with clearing
house records as each trade may be traced back to a code number
and reveal whether settlement regulations between broker-client
It will also reveal the particular shares being traded by
the clients, in what quantities and when.
